title: Elastic Capacity Projection Tool v1
summary: Working calculator to translate per-customer throughput profiles and burst behavior into a monthly capacity plan that feeds the Optimize cost model. Focus is on elastic (ephemeral) capacity sizing vs reserved pools, and the interaction of batching, prefix caching, and quantization on per-token cost. This is an early internal tool for product + infra to iterate on assumptions before adding to the canonical workbook.
sheet_tabs: Overview - high level summary + charts (text export)
Customer Profiles - seg by SLA, p95 qps traces
Hourly Simulation - synthetic traffic generator and hour-by-hour utilization
Instance Sizing - mapping QPS -> GPU type & count
Cost Outputs - monthly unit economics, reserved vs burst comparison
Sensitivity - run scenarios and tornado results
assumptions: Billing granularity: per-minute allocation for reserved; per-second for ephemerals (normalized to $/hour in calc)
Average tokens per request: baseline 180 tokens (user+assistant). adjustable per-profile
Batching efficiency: 0.65 effective token throughput for mixed traffic unless pinned low-latency path
Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): default 12% overall, higher for templated prompts
Quantization savings: 30% cost reduction on specific model variants when applied; performance tradeoffs included
Autoscale cold-start: 45s median to first token for cold ephemeral GPU allocation
SLAs: Premium customers require p95 latency < 200ms under normal load; impacts sizing
key_metrics: Reserved utilization % (hours reserved used / hours reserved purchased)
Headroom margin required for 95% SLA compliance
Cost delta: reserve vs burst (monthly, 95th percentile basis)
inputs_table: Monthly active customers,80000,users,Used to derive per-customer QPS distribution
% premium customers,12,%,Influences SLA and required headroom
Avg calls per user per month,35,calls/month,Use to estimate baseline QPS and diurnal shape
Peak hour multiplier,4,x,Ratio peak hour qps to average hour
p95 qps per premium customer at peak,0.12,qps,Measured from early customers; distribution modeled in Customer Profiles
Tokens per call,180,tokens,Includes assistant output; adjustable by profile
GPU types cost/hr (A100 equiv),8.5,$/hr,Normalized using cloud pricing and Ampere equivalence

sensitivity_scenarios: Conservative growth: +10% MAU, cache +5pp, quantization off -> Monthly cost $142,000; reserve utilization 68%
Aggressive growth: +40% MAU, cache -3pp, quantization on selective models -> Monthly cost $223,000; reserve utilization 82%
High-latency-avoidance (tight SLA): reserve +30% headroom, lower batching -> Monthly cost $188,000; ephemeral usage reduced but unit cost increases
Bursty enterprise onboarding: 5 large enterprise customers with spiky traffic -> requires additional ephemeral capacity, cost delta +22% relative to smooth profile
instance_mapping_notes: Map QPS to instance types using median tokens/s after batching and KV cache hit reduction
Fallback rule: if predicted cold ephemerals needed > 3 GPU in 5-minute window, prefer temporary warm pool for faster response
Prefer quantized model variants for low-cost tiers where quality impact < 0.8 on evaluation set
